newsitem.title: USA: Calif. disability insurance tax rate cut-Governor.
newsitem.headline: Calif. disability insurance tax rate cut-Governor.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson said Tuesday the tax rate for more than 10 million California workers covered by the state disability insurance program would be cut on Jan 1.
Wilson said the tax rate would drop to 0.5 percent, the lowest rate in the 50 years history of the disability insurance program.

The lowered rate should provide an additional $662 million of spendable income for California workers in 1997 and would provide three year cumulative savings of $3.5 billion, Wilson said in a statement.
Wilson said the disability insurance fund has built a healthy balance as a result of recent legislative reforms. The fund is expected to end 1996 with a balance of $1.7 billion.
The maximum 1997 contribution will be 0.5 percent of the first $31,767 in wages, or a maximum of $159.

The disability insurance program pays benefits to workers who are disabled due to non-work related illness or injury. Benefits range from $50 to $336 per week for a maximum of 52 weeks, depending on earnings.
